MPE-FMT-002.title: Byte order
MPE-FMT-002.sentence: The MPE client library shall encode every multi-byte integer in the Visible Header and the Sealed Prefix in big-endian byte order.
MPE-FMT-002.verify: test: `expiry` = 0x01020304 encodes as bytes 01 02 03 04 at offset 4.

MPE-FMT-003.title: Visible fields
MPE-FMT-003.sentence: Outside the Sealed Body, the MPE client library shall place only `version`, `size_class`, `shard`, `reserved`, `expiry` and the Admission Slot, at the offsets in the Visible Header table.
MPE-FMT-003.verify: inspection; test: 10^4 Prototype Envelopes each have a header of 8 + P-FMT-2 bytes, and no plaintext outside the header, the Admission Slot, the Sealed Body's `MPE-FMT-051` clear prefix (salt, nonce, Recognition Tag) and the authenticator.

MPE-FMT-004.title: No identity-derived visible values
MPE-FMT-004.sentence: Outside the Sealed Body, the MPE client library shall place no value derived from a stream identifier, a recipient key or a Publisher long-term key. The `shard` field is the only exception.
MPE-FMT-004.verify: test: within each size class, compare 1,000 Envelopes from one Publisher and stream with 1,000 from distinct Publishers and streams; outside `shard` and `expiry`, the largest per-offset chi-square statistic, with its p-value from 1,000 random relabellings of the two samples, stays above the 1 percent family-wise level, and a planted constant byte at one offset of the single-Publisher sample is flagged.

MPE-FMT-005.title: Admission Slot unlinkability
MPE-FMT-005.sentence: The MPE client library shall place no value in the Admission Slot that is constant across one Publisher's MPE Envelopes and differs between Publishers.
MPE-FMT-005.verify: test: two memberships send 100 Envelopes each in one admission window. No Admission Slot byte range is constant within one membership and different between the two.

MPE-FMT-006.title: Reserved bytes
MPE-FMT-006.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope has a non-zero reserved byte, then the Bus Node shall return Reject.
MPE-FMT-006.verify: test: set each reserved bit of a valid vector in turn; each result is Reject.

MPE-FMT-007.title: Exact length
MPE-FMT-007.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope's length differs from 8 + P-FMT-2 + the P-FMT-1 body length of its `size_class`, then the Bus Node shall return Reject.
MPE-FMT-007.verify: test: valid vectors shortened by 1 B or lengthened by 1 B are Rejected.

MPE-FMT-008.title: Unknown size class
MPE-FMT-008.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope's `size_class` has no entry in P-FMT-1, then the Bus Node shall return Reject.

MPE-FMT-009.title: Structural checks first
MPE-FMT-009.sentence: The Bus Node shall complete the version, reserved-byte, size-class, length and expiry checks on an MPE Envelope before it runs any cryptographic verification on it.
MPE-FMT-009.verify: test: send 10^4 malformed Envelopes with well-formed Admission Slots; the verification counter stays at 0.

MPE-FMT-010.title: Transmit size bound
MPE-FMT-010.sentence: The Bus Node shall set the GossipSub encoded RPC limit (`max_transmit_size`) to P-FMT-6 bytes, separately from the MPE Envelope length check.
MPE-FMT-010.verify: test: an encoded RPC of P-FMT-6 + 1 bytes never reaches the validator; an MPE Envelope of a wrong length inside a smaller RPC is rejected by the application check.

MPE-FMT-011.title: Body-blind validation
MPE-FMT-011.sentence: The Bus Node shall compute every validation outcome without decrypting or parsing the Sealed Body.
MPE-FMT-011.verify: inspection: the validator links no AEAD or schema decoder. Test: Envelopes with random Sealed Bodies and valid admission get the same outcome as real ones.

MPE-FMT-012.title: GossipSub carriage
MPE-FMT-012.sentence: The Bus Node shall publish each MPE Envelope as the whole GossipSub `data` field, with the `from`, `seqno`, `signature` and `key` fields absent.
MPE-FMT-012.verify: test: captured RPC frames lack all four fields, and peers in Anonymous mode accept them.

MPE-FMT-013.title: Sealed Body length
MPE-FMT-013.sentence: The MPE client library shall produce a Sealed Body whose length equals the P-FMT-1 entry for the MPE Envelope's `size_class`.
MPE-FMT-013.verify: test: every Prototype Envelope has a body length listed in P-FMT-1 that matches its class byte.

MPE-FMT-014.title: Smallest fitting class
MPE-FMT-014.sentence: When publishing a Message, the MPE client library shall select the smallest size class whose payload capacity holds the payload, unless the application names a larger class.
MPE-FMT-014.verify: test: payloads exactly at each class capacity, and 1 B over it, land in the expected classes.

MPE-FMT-015.title: Oversize payload
MPE-FMT-015.sentence: If a Message payload exceeds the payload capacity of the largest size class, then the MPE client library shall return a payload-too-large error and publish no MPE Envelope.
MPE-FMT-015.verify: test: a payload of capacity + 1 B returns the error, and no Envelope reaches the mesh.

MPE-FMT-016.title: Sealed padding
MPE-FMT-016.sentence: The MPE client library shall place all padding inside the authenticated encryption, so that Messages of different payload lengths in one size class produce MPE Envelopes of equal length.
MPE-FMT-016.verify: test: in each class, a 1 B payload and a full-capacity payload give equal wire lengths.

MPE-FMT-017.title: Padding check
MPE-FMT-017.sentence: If the padding of an opened Message contains a non-zero byte, then the MPE client library shall discard the Message as malformed.
MPE-FMT-017.verify: test: a vector re-sealed with one pad byte set to 0x01 is discarded and counted.

MPE-FMT-018.title: Envelope Identifier
MPE-FMT-018.sentence: The MPE client library shall compute the MPE Envelope Identifier as SHA-256 over the P-FMT-11 domain string, the Network Identifier, Visible Header bytes 0 to 7 and the Sealed Body, excluding the Admission Slot.
MPE-FMT-018.verify: test vectors; test: one body under two different Admission Slots yields one identifier.

MPE-FMT-019.title: GossipSub message id
MPE-FMT-019.sentence: The Bus Node shall use the GossipSub message identifier of MPE-NET-010, which hashes every MPE Envelope byte and therefore differs from the MPE Envelope Identifier.
MPE-FMT-019.verify: test: two Envelopes differing only in the Admission Slot get distinct message identifiers and one Envelope Identifier.

MPE-FMT-020.title: Acyclic construction
MPE-FMT-020.sentence: The MPE client library shall build an MPE Envelope in this order: Sealed Body, then MPE Envelope Identifier, then Admission Slot. No step takes input from a later step.
MPE-FMT-020.verify: inspection; test vectors rebuild each stage from earlier stages only.

MPE-FMT-021.title: Network binding
MPE-FMT-021.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope was admitted under a different Network Identifier, then the Bus Node shall return Reject.
MPE-FMT-021.verify: test: an Envelope valid on a test network is Rejected by a Bus Node configured with a different genesis hash.

MPE-FMT-022.title: Logical Message Identifier
MPE-FMT-022.sentence: The MPE client library shall seal a random 16-byte Logical Message Identifier that is the same in every retransmission and every carrier of one Message.
MPE-FMT-022.verify: test: one Message sent on the overlay and on the mock ledger carrier opens with equal Logical Message Identifiers.

MPE-FMT-023.title: Version bound to GossipSub topic
MPE-FMT-023.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope's `version` differs from the supported version assigned to the GossipSub topic it arrived on, then the Bus Node shall return Reject.
MPE-FMT-023.verify: test: `version` = 2 on a supported v1 GossipSub topic is Rejected and lowers the forwarding peer's P₄ score; validity that cannot be determined for lack of protocol support follows MPE-SEC-008 (Ignore).

MPE-FMT-024.title: Version overlap
MPE-FMT-024.sentence: Where two MPE Envelope versions are active, the Bus Node shall relay the GossipSub topics of both versions for at least P-FMT-9 after the newer version activates.
MPE-FMT-024.verify: simulation, upgrade half the nodes; no unexpired old-version Envelope is lost during the window.

MPE-FMT-025.title: Unsupported sealed format
MPE-FMT-025.sentence: If an opened Sealed Prefix has an unknown `pt_version` or `kind`, then the MPE client library shall return a typed unsupported-format error to the application.
MPE-FMT-025.verify: test: vectors with `pt_version` = 2 or with an undefined `kind` return the typed error.

MPE-FMT-026.title: Unknown schema
MPE-FMT-026.sentence: When the MPE client library opens a Message whose schema identifier has no registered decoder, the MPE client library shall deliver the Message to the application marked as undecodable.
MPE-FMT-026.verify: test: a Message with an unregistered schema arrives flagged as undecodable, with its raw payload.

MPE-FMT-027.title: Static decoder dispatch
MPE-FMT-027.sentence: The MPE client library shall select a payload decoder only from a table that is keyed by schema identifier and fixed when the application registers.
MPE-FMT-027.verify: inspection: no eval, reflection or dynamic loading keyed by payload bytes; fuzz test of the decoder path.

MPE-FMT-028.title: Expiry field
MPE-FMT-028.sentence: The MPE client library shall set `expiry` to an unsigned 32-bit Unix time in seconds, no later than its own clock plus P-FMT-3.
MPE-FMT-028.verify: test: at creation, Prototype Envelopes satisfy `now < expiry ≤ now + P-FMT-3`.

MPE-FMT-029.title: Expiry too far ahead
MPE-FMT-029.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope's `expiry` exceeds the Bus Node's clock plus P-FMT-3 plus P-FMT-4, then the Bus Node shall return Reject.
MPE-FMT-029.verify: test: `expiry` = now + P-FMT-3 + P-FMT-4 + 1 s is Rejected; one second less is not.

MPE-FMT-030.title: Expired on arrival
MPE-FMT-030.sentence: If a received MPE Envelope's `expiry` is earlier than the Bus Node's clock minus P-FMT-4, then the Bus Node shall return Ignore.
MPE-FMT-030.verify: test: an expired Envelope is not forwarded, and the sender's P₄ counter does not change.

MPE-FMT-031.title: Unsafe clock
MPE-FMT-031.sentence: While the Ledger Adapter view is stale under MPE-NET-019, the Bus Node shall return Ignore instead of Reject for an MPE Envelope that fails the expiry check of MPE-FMT-029.
MPE-FMT-031.verify: test, shift the mock adapter timestamp by P-NET-13 + 1 s; far-future expiry yields Ignore and valid Envelopes are still accepted.

MPE-FMT-032.title: No forwarding after expiry
MPE-FMT-032.sentence: When an MPE Envelope's `expiry` passes, the Bus Node shall stop sending that MPE Envelope to peers, including IWANT responses and sends already queued.
MPE-FMT-032.verify: test: an IWANT for an expired identifier and a send queued before expiry both transmit nothing; a conformance test is recorded for each transport implementation, because stock GossipSub message caches do not read the MPE expiry field.

MPE-FMT-033.title: Lifetime ceiling
MPE-FMT-033.sentence: The Bus Registry shall reject any P-FMT-3 parameter value above 1,209,600 s.
MPE-FMT-033.verify: test on the Bus Registry model: a parameter change to 1,209,601 s fails.

MPE-FMT-034.title: Sealed Prefix
MPE-FMT-034.sentence: The MPE client library shall begin every Sealed Body plaintext with the Sealed Prefix fields `pt_version`, `kind`, `flags`, `payload_len`, `schema_version`, `seq`, Logical Message Identifier and schema identifier.
MPE-FMT-034.verify: inspection; test vectors decode every field.

MPE-FMT-035.title: Sealed control packets
MPE-FMT-035.sentence: The MPE client library shall carry every session or group control packet, including any MLS framing, entirely inside a Sealed Body.
MPE-FMT-035.verify: inspection; test: no MLS header byte appears outside the Sealed Body.

MPE-FMT-036.title: No receipt kind
MPE-FMT-036.sentence: The MPE client library shall define no MPE Envelope `kind` whose purpose is to acknowledge receipt to a Publisher.

MPE-FMT-037.title: Carrier-independent body
MPE-FMT-037.sentence: The MPE client library shall open a Sealed Body using only its bytes, the `version`, the `size_class` and the recipient's key material.
MPE-FMT-037.verify: test: a body taken from the mock ledger carrier opens exactly as its overlay copy does.

MPE-FMT-038.title: Explicit external fetch
MPE-FMT-038.sentence: The MPE client library shall not retrieve an object referenced inside a Message unless the application calls an explicit fetch operation.
MPE-FMT-038.verify: test: receiving a Message that contains a reference produces no outbound request.

MPE-FMT-039.title: Optional fragmentation
MPE-FMT-039.sentence: Where sealed fragmentation is enabled, the MPE client library shall deliver a fragmented Message only after all of its fragments (at most P-FMT-7) have been opened.
MPE-FMT-039.verify: test: drop one of 16 fragments; nothing is delivered, and the partial set expires.

MPE-FMT-040.title: Constant `Misc` name for ledger-lane parts
MPE-FMT-040.sentence: The MPE client library shall set the `Misc` `name` of every part of a ledger-lane MPE Envelope to the P-FMT-10 envelope name `mip-xxxx:envelope[v1]`, NUL-padded to 32 bytes.
MPE-FMT-040.verify: test: all parts from two different streams carry byte-identical 32-byte `name` fields equal to `mip-xxxx:envelope[v1]` followed by NUL bytes.

MPE-FMT-041.title: Part split
MPE-FMT-041.sentence: The MPE client library shall carry a class-c Sealed Body on the ledger as 4^c `Misc` events whose 256-byte payloads, concatenated in emission order, equal that body.
MPE-FMT-041.verify: test vectors for classes 0 to 2 against the mock Ledger Adapter.

MPE-FMT-042.title: One phase of one intent
MPE-FMT-042.sentence: The MPE client library shall emit all parts of one ledger-lane MPE Envelope within one execution phase of one intent.
MPE-FMT-042.verify: inspection of the built transactions: all parts of an Envelope sit in one segment, guaranteed or fallible (a 16-part call exceeds the guaranteed-segment budget); ledger-9 devnet test with a failing fallible segment shows that no part of that Envelope is applied.

MPE-FMT-043.title: One `Misc` per part
MPE-FMT-043.sentence: The MPE client library shall emit each ledger part as one `Misc` event whose struct data is 288 bytes: a 32-byte name and a 256-byte payload.
MPE-FMT-043.verify: inspection of the contract; test: every emitted `Misc` carries 288 bytes of struct data; the serialized size, about 40 bytes larger by MIP-0002's estimate, is measured under MPE-PRF-040.

MPE-FMT-044.title: Ledger part limit
MPE-FMT-044.sentence: If an application asks for ledger carriage of an MPE Envelope that needs more than P-FMT-8 parts, then the MPE client library shall return an error without building a transaction.
MPE-FMT-044.verify: test: a request for ledger-lane carriage of a class-3 Envelope returns the error and submits nothing; analysis: the proving circuit size of the largest permitted call is stated (16 parts in one call is k = 22 with 2,651,779 rows; 4 parts is k = 20) under MPE-PRF-043.

MPE-FMT-045.title: Ledger reassembly
MPE-FMT-045.sentence: When reading ledger-carried MPE Envelopes, the MPE client library shall concatenate, in ledger emission order, the payloads of parts named P-FMT-10 that come from one transaction and one physical intent.
MPE-FMT-045.verify: test: interleaved parts from two intents in one block reassemble into two bodies.

MPE-FMT-046.title: Malformed ledger group
MPE-FMT-046.sentence: If a reassembled ledger group has a part count that is not 4^c for a defined class c, then the MPE client library shall discard the group as malformed.
MPE-FMT-046.verify: test: groups of 2, 3 and 5 parts are discarded and counted.

MPE-FMT-047.title: Anchor notification event
MPE-FMT-047.sentence: The Bus Registry shall emit each Anchor as one `Misc` event named `mip-xxxx:anchor[v1]`, NUL-padded to 32 bytes, whose payload is the MPE-NET-050 Anchor payload.
MPE-FMT-047.verify: ledger-9 devnet test: each Anchor transaction produces exactly one `Misc` with that name and a 256-byte payload; consumers verify Anchors against Bus Registry state (MPE-CON-016), not against this event.

MPE-FMT-048.title: Admission Slot measurement
MPE-FMT-048.sentence: The Prototype shall measure the serialised length of the chosen Admission Proof and record it as P-FMT-2 before any P-FMT-1 value is frozen.
MPE-FMT-048.verify: demonstration: a benchmark report giving the measured length and the proof system used.

MPE-FMT-049.title: Test vectors
MPE-FMT-049.sentence: The Prototype shall publish byte-exact test vectors for each size class, the Sealed Prefix, the MPE Envelope Identifier, the binding between Admission Slot and identifier, and the ledger part split.
MPE-FMT-049.verify: test: an independent decoder reproduces every vector.

MPE-CRY-001.title: Default cryptographic profile
MPE-CRY-001.sentence: The MPE client library shall implement, as suite 0x01, an invitation-based symmetric profile using HKDF-SHA-256 key derivation, HMAC-SHA-256 recognition, ChaCha20-Poly1305 sealing and plain Ed25519 publisher authentication.
MPE-CRY-001.verify: test, independent implementations agree on derivation, sealing, recognition and signature vectors, and every Envelope of this profile carries suite identifier 0x01.

MPE-CRY-002.title: Sealed application metadata
MPE-CRY-002.sentence: The MPE client library shall encrypt the Message’s private stream identifier, publisher identity, schema, logical identifier, sequence, application timestamps, payload and publisher signature inside the MPE Envelope.
MPE-CRY-002.verify: inspection, the wire-field inventory contains these fields only within authenticated ciphertext.

MPE-CRY-003.title: Authenticated padding
MPE-CRY-003.sentence: The MPE client library shall include the padding prescribed by the MPE Envelope’s size class within authenticated encryption.
MPE-CRY-003.verify: test, changing any protected padding byte causes authentication failure.

MPE-CRY-004.title: Public-context authentication
MPE-CRY-004.sentence: The MPE client library shall authenticate the Network Identifier, Visible Header bytes 0 to 3 and the Sealed Body's salt, nonce and Recognition Tag as AEAD associated data, and bind Visible Header bytes 4 to 7 by fixing `expiry` at creation plus 172,800 s and covering creation and expiry in the signed statement.
MPE-CRY-004.verify: test, changing any associated byte prevents opening; changing `expiry` changes the MPE Envelope Identifier and fails the Subscriber's comparison with the signed expiry.

MPE-CRY-005.title: Acyclic Envelope construction
MPE-CRY-005.sentence: The MPE client library shall construct an MPE Envelope through the dependency order pre-seal header, signed plaintext, ciphertext, admission content commitment, Admission Proof, then final wire identifier.
MPE-CRY-005.verify: inspection, the construction dependency graph is acyclic and every cryptographic input exists before use.

MPE-CRY-006.title: Domain separation
MPE-CRY-006.sentence: The MPE client library shall separate Recognition Tags, encryption keys, associated data, publisher signatures, MPE Envelope identifiers, receipts, admission values and consumption nullifiers with the distinct version-1 labels of the MPE-CRY-042 table, binding the Network Identifier and the cryptographic profile where that table's construction includes them.
MPE-CRY-006.verify: test, cross-purpose, cross-network and cross-profile substitution vectors fail; inspection, every label in the code appears in the MPE-CRY-042 table.

MPE-CRY-007.title: Purpose-specific derivation
MPE-CRY-007.sentence: The MPE client library shall derive separate recognition and encryption keys from a stream secret using distinct HKDF-SHA-256 purpose labels, with the MPE Envelope salt included in per-Envelope encryption derivation.
MPE-CRY-007.verify: test, derivation vectors distinguish purposes, salts, networks and profiles.

MPE-CRY-008.title: Random stream secrets
MPE-CRY-008.sentence: When a private stream is created, the MPE client library shall obtain its P-CRY-1-byte stream secret from the operating-system cryptographic random-number interface.
MPE-CRY-008.verify: inspection, stream creation requests exactly P-CRY-1 bytes from the configured interface (getrandom on Linux); test, an injected interface failure produces the MPE-CRY-009 result.

MPE-CRY-009.title: Randomness failure
MPE-CRY-009.sentence: If required cryptographic randomness cannot be obtained, then the MPE client library shall refuse the affected cryptographic operation with a local failure result.
MPE-CRY-009.verify: test, injected entropy failure produces no key, ciphertext or bootstrap publication.

MPE-CRY-010.title: Nonce uniqueness
MPE-CRY-010.sentence: The MPE client library shall use each AEAD key–nonce pair for at most one encryption operation.
MPE-CRY-010.verify: test, forced nonce repetition, concurrent publication and crash recovery cannot produce a second encryption under the same pair.

MPE-CRY-011.title: Unsafe restored state
MPE-CRY-011.sentence: If restored client state cannot establish nonce uniqueness or ratchet-state freshness, then the MPE client library shall refuse publication under the affected key generation until authenticated re-establishment.
MPE-CRY-011.verify: test, restoring a pre-publication snapshot prevents subsequent publication under its obsolete generation.

MPE-CRY-012.title: Exact retransmission
MPE-CRY-012.sentence: When an existing MPE Envelope is retransmitted, the MPE client library shall reuse its original serialized bytes.
MPE-CRY-012.verify: test, repeated transmission preserves ciphertext, nonce, Recognition Tag and wire identifier.

MPE-CRY-013.title: Salted Recognition Tags
MPE-CRY-013.sentence: When sealing a Message, the MPE client library shall generate a P-CRY-2-byte Recognition Tag by truncating HMAC-SHA-256 over the canonical Recognition Tag domain and a fresh P-CRY-3-byte MPE Envelope salt under the stream’s recognition key.
MPE-CRY-013.verify: test, independent vectors agree; arbitrary publisher-sequence gaps do not prevent recognition under a retained stream key.

MPE-CRY-014.title: Recognition is provisional
MPE-CRY-014.sentence: When a Recognition Tag or fuzzy clue matches, the MPE client library shall treat the MPE Envelope only as a candidate for complete Message authentication.
MPE-CRY-014.verify: test, matching hints paired with invalid ciphertext or signatures produce no Message delivery.

MPE-CRY-015.title: Local Recognition Tag matching
MPE-CRY-015.sentence: The MPE client library shall perform Recognition Tag matching within the Subscriber’s local trust boundary.
MPE-CRY-015.verify: inspection, Bus Node and Store Node interfaces receive neither Recognition Tag keys nor Recognition Tag match results.

MPE-CRY-016.title: Recognition-key bound
MPE-CRY-016.sentence: When installing subscription state would exceed P-CRY-4 distinct recognition keys, the MPE client library shall reject that installation with a local capacity result.
MPE-CRY-016.verify: test, installation at the limit succeeds; installation beyond the limit leaves existing subscriptions unchanged.

MPE-CRY-017.title: Ambiguous opening
MPE-CRY-017.sentence: If one MPE Envelope authenticates as belonging to distinct private streams, then the MPE client library shall reject its delivery with a local ambiguity result.
MPE-CRY-017.verify: test, injected multiple-opening vectors produce no delivery to either stream.

MPE-CRY-018.title: Authenticated invitations
MPE-CRY-018.sentence: When installing a private subscription, the MPE client library shall validate an invitation binding the network, cryptographic profile, stream secret or setup material, and authorized publisher keys through the configured authenticated invitation channel.
MPE-CRY-018.verify: test, modified, unauthenticated, foreign-network and unsupported-profile invitations cannot install subscriptions.

MPE-CRY-019.title: Revocation rekeying
MPE-CRY-019.sentence: When an authorized membership change removes a Subscriber from a symmetric private stream, the MPE client library shall generate the replacement stream secret independently of the previous stream secret.
MPE-CRY-019.verify: test, possession of the old secret does not derive the replacement secret or open Messages sealed under it.

MPE-CRY-020.title: Publisher signature profile
MPE-CRY-020.sentence: The MPE client library shall authenticate publisher statements with plain Ed25519 in the default cryptographic profile.
MPE-CRY-020.verify: test, library signatures verify over identical statement bytes in a compiled Compact fixture; analysis, consumption-circuit rows, proving time and prover-key size under Ed25519 and JubJub Schnorr (MPE-CRY-043) decide the production profile.

MPE-CRY-021.title: Signed statement binding
MPE-CRY-021.sentence: The MPE client library shall sign a canonical statement binding the signature domain, pre-seal-header digest, private stream identifier, logical identifier, publisher sequence, schema, creation time, expiry, payload digest and applicable destination contract and action.
MPE-CRY-021.verify: test, substituting each signed field causes publisher-signature verification failure.

MPE-CRY-022.title: Authenticated delivery
MPE-CRY-022.sentence: When an MPE Envelope is opened, the MPE client library shall deliver its Message only after validation of the seal, canonical inner encoding, signed context, authorized publisher key and application expiry.
MPE-CRY-022.verify: test, malformed, expired, unauthorized and signature-invalid Messages produce no delivery.

MPE-CRY-023.title: Failure-atomic cryptographic state
MPE-CRY-023.sentence: When processing an incoming MPE Envelope, the MPE client library shall commit cryptographic state changes only after complete Message authentication succeeds.
MPE-CRY-023.verify: test, invalid bodies following valid-looking headers leave persistent cryptographic state unchanged.

MPE-CRY-024.title: Authenticated logical replay
MPE-CRY-024.sentence: If an authenticated Message’s publisher, private stream and logical identifier tuple is already present in durable replay state, then the MPE client library shall suppress its repeat delivery.
MPE-CRY-024.verify: test, independently encrypted retries of one authenticated logical Message produce one delivery across restart.

MPE-CRY-025.title: Secret-bearing consumption nullifiers
MPE-CRY-025.sentence: Where contract-consumption nullifier derivation is supported, the MPE client library shall derive the consumption nullifier from a Message-specific secret using a canonical domain containing the network and destination contract.
MPE-CRY-025.verify: test, the same Message secret reproduces the destination’s consumption nullifier; changing destination changes it.

MPE-CRY-026.title: Explicit security posture
MPE-CRY-026.sentence: The MPE client library shall expose each profile’s capability record specifying content forward secrecy, key-retention exposure, post-compromise recovery conditions, passive quantum protection, authentication algorithm and metadata-forward-secrecy limitations.
MPE-CRY-026.verify: inspection, capability records distinguish the default from ratcheted profiles and state all retained-key exposure.

MPE-CRY-027.title: Wallet-derived admission and invitation keys
MPE-CRY-027.sentence: Where wallet-seed derivation is supported, the MPE client library shall derive only the admission secret and invitation identity keys from the seed, through `deriveSecret` with domains `mpe:admission:v1` and `mpe:invitation:v1` and the Network Identifier, the Bus Registry contract address and the membership period as context.
MPE-CRY-027.verify: inspection, derivation paths cannot reconstruct erasable session state from the wallet seed; test with a `deriveSecret` stub: a restored wallet recovers the same admission secret and membership, no derived value equals a spending or encryption key, and a wallet without `deriveSecret` falls back to MPE-ECO-006 generation.

MPE-CRY-028.title: Encrypted-header session profile
MPE-CRY-028.sentence: Where ratcheted pairwise sessions are supported, the MPE client library shall seal the complete encrypted-header Double Ratchet packet within the MPE Envelope’s protected representation.
MPE-CRY-028.verify: inspection, packet captures contain no clear ratchet header or stable session identifier.

MPE-CRY-029.title: Ratchet-key erasure
MPE-CRY-029.sentence: When a ratcheted session transition becomes durable, the MPE client library shall erase superseded secret state outside the declared skipped-key retention policy.
MPE-CRY-029.verify: inspection, post-transition memory and persistent-state inventories exclude used message keys and obsolete ratchet secrets.

MPE-CRY-030.title: Bounded skipped-key retention
MPE-CRY-030.sentence: While a ratcheted session is active, the MPE client library shall retain skipped-message keys only within P-CRY-5 derivations per transition, P-CRY-6 stored keys per device and P-CRY-7 seconds after derivation.
MPE-CRY-030.verify: test, boundary gaps and clock advancement enforce every limit without retaining excess keys.

MPE-CRY-031.title: Explicit cryptographic gaps
MPE-CRY-031.sentence: If opening a Message requires erased keys or would exceed a cryptographic key budget, then the MPE client library shall return a local resynchronization-required result.
MPE-CRY-031.verify: test, over-limit and erased-key back-fill produces an explicit result without reconstructing obsolete state.

MPE-CRY-032.title: Hybrid session establishment
MPE-CRY-032.sentence: Where the hybrid pairwise profile is supported, the MPE client library shall establish sessions using PQXDH instantiated with X25519 and ML-KEM-768, with network, profile, identities and actual KEM public key bound to the bootstrap transcript.
MPE-CRY-032.verify: test, independent bootstrap vectors agree; identity, KEM-key, network and profile substitutions fail.

MPE-CRY-033.title: Wrapped bootstrap metadata
MPE-CRY-033.sentence: Where invitation-based hybrid establishment is supported, the MPE client library shall protect bootstrap identity keys, prekey identifiers and initialization material with invitation-derived wrapping keys.
MPE-CRY-033.verify: inspection, bootstrap captures reveal no identity key or prekey identifier outside the protected representation.

MPE-CRY-034.title: One-time prekey consumption
MPE-CRY-034.sentence: When a bootstrap authenticates successfully, the MPE client library shall erase its used one-time prekey private material after durably recording that bootstrap’s identity.
MPE-CRY-034.verify: test, concurrent duplicate bootstraps and restart yield at most one initialization and no remaining consumed private prekey.

MPE-CRY-035.title: Establishment failure
MPE-CRY-035.sentence: If required one-time prekeys are exhausted, bootstrap authentication fails or selected-profile input validation fails, then the MPE client library shall refuse establishment without selecting a weaker profile.
MPE-CRY-035.verify: test, exhausted, corrupted and downgrade vectors create no session under any alternative profile.

MPE-CRY-036.title: Cryptographic size and cost report
MPE-CRY-036.sentence: The Prototype shall report serialized cryptographic component sizes, complete MPE Envelope sizes, usable payload capacity, operation-time distributions and peak cryptographic-state bytes for every implemented profile at its configured key limits.
MPE-CRY-036.verify: demonstration, a reproducible report accounts for every serialized byte and gives operation times in microseconds and state sizes in bytes.

MPE-CRY-037.title: Fuzzy-detection activation
MPE-CRY-037.sentence: When initializing a client configuration without explicit first-contact FMD opt-in, the MPE client library shall leave fuzzy detection disabled.
MPE-CRY-037.verify: test, default configurations generate no fuzzy clue or delegated detection registration.

MPE-CRY-038.title: Restricted detection delegation
MPE-CRY-038.sentence: Where first-contact FMD delegation is enabled, the MPE client library shall export only the selected construction’s first-contact detection capability to the detector.
MPE-CRY-038.verify: inspection, detector registration contains only construction-defined first-contact detection material.

MPE-CRY-039.title: FMD construction measurement
MPE-CRY-039.sentence: Where experimental FMD2 is implemented, the Prototype shall report clue size, generation time, testing time, true-match failures and observed unrelated-clue match frequency at P-CRY-8.
MPE-CRY-039.verify: demonstration, a labeled-corpus report states sample counts, configuration, hardware and frequency uncertainty.

MPE-CRY-040.title: Production composition gate
MPE-CRY-040.sentence: MPE shall admit a cryptographic profile to production only after independent review accepts its confidentiality, recognition key hiding, ambiguity handling, nonce lifecycle, replay rules and implemented protocol composition.
MPE-CRY-040.verify: inspection, the review covers exact profile bytes and vectors, with no unresolved critical or high findings under its stated severity rubric.

MPE-PUB-001.title: Stream identifiers sealed
MPE-PUB-001.sentence: The MPE client library shall place every stream identifier, session identifier and recipient identifier only inside the sealed body of an MPE Envelope.
MPE-PUB-001.verify: test. Publish 10,000 Envelopes on 100 streams. Bus Node captures contain none of the stream, session or recipient identifiers as byte strings.

MPE-PUB-002.title: Shard derivation
MPE-PUB-002.sentence: The MPE client library shall set an MPE Envelope's Shard to a domain-separated SHA-256 hash of the audience key reduced modulo P-PUB-1 as read from the Bus Registry.
MPE-PUB-002.verify: test, vectors for 1,000 keys at P-PUB-1 of 1 and 8 match a reference implementation.

MPE-PUB-003.title: Bus Node shard-count transition
MPE-PUB-003.sentence: When the Bus Registry changes P-PUB-1, the Bus Node shall accept MPE Envelopes placed under either the previous or the new value until `L_max` plus P-PUB-8 has elapsed after the change takes effect.
MPE-PUB-003.verify: simulation. Change from 1 to 8 Shards under load. No Envelope is rejected for a shard mismatch during the transition.

MPE-PUB-004.title: Client shard-count transition
MPE-PUB-004.sentence: When the Bus Registry changes P-PUB-1, the MPE client library shall follow each audience key's Shards under both the previous and the new value until `L_max` plus P-PUB-8 has elapsed after the change takes effect.
MPE-PUB-004.verify: simulation. No Message is lost across a change from 1 to 8 Shards.

MPE-PUB-005.title: Per-Envelope Recognition Tag
MPE-PUB-005.sentence: The MPE client library shall compute each MPE Envelope's Recognition Tag as a keyed pseudorandom function of the audience key and a fresh random salt carried in that MPE Envelope.
MPE-PUB-005.verify: test. Across 10⁶ Envelopes under one key, no Recognition Tag repeats and a chi-square test does not reject uniform Recognition Tag bytes at α = 0.01. Inspection: a cryptographic review of the construction.

MPE-PUB-006.title: Random private audience keys
MPE-PUB-006.sentence: The MPE client library shall obtain every private audience key as 32 bytes from the operating-system cryptographic random-number interface.
MPE-PUB-006.verify: inspection, the API offers no passphrase input for private streams and key generation calls the operating-system interface.

MPE-PUB-007.title: Public stream key
MPE-PUB-007.sentence: Where a stream is public, the MPE client library shall derive its audience key as a domain-separated hash of the published stream name.
MPE-PUB-007.verify: test. Known-answer vectors. Public and private Envelopes cannot be told apart by any header field.

MPE-PUB-008.title: Invitation-only private membership
MPE-PUB-008.sentence: The MPE client library shall add a private stream to a Subscriber only by importing an invitation received outside the bus.
MPE-PUB-008.verify: inspection. The API exposes no other way in. Test: an Envelope sent under an unregistered recipient key is never surfaced.

MPE-PUB-009.title: No subscriber directory
MPE-PUB-009.sentence: MPE shall provide no Bus Node, Store Node or Bus Registry operation that returns which Subscribers follow a stream, Recognition Tag or audience key.
MPE-PUB-009.verify: inspection of the protocol identifiers and Bus Registry entry points.
MPE-PUB-009.note: This excludes, by design, the indexer-side relevance model that MPS-0005 plans for private events: per-wallet relevance tables and wallet-session decryption at the Indexer.

MPE-PUB-010.title: Local recognition
MPE-PUB-010.sentence: The MPE client library shall not send any audience key, recognition key or Recognition Tag filter to a Bus Node, Store Node or Indexer.
MPE-PUB-010.verify: test. Capture all client egress for 24 h. No key or Recognition Tag filter material appears.
MPE-PUB-010.note: This excludes, by design, the per-wallet relevance and session-decryption model that MPS-0005 plans for the Indexer.

MPE-PUB-011.title: Full-Shard reception
MPE-PUB-011.sentence: While in the default reception mode, the MPE client library shall retrieve every unexpired MPE Envelope of each Shard it follows.
MPE-PUB-011.verify: simulation. The count received equals the Shard's publication count minus expired Envelopes.

MPE-PUB-012.title: Network behaviour independent of recognition
MPE-PUB-012.sentence: The MPE client library shall send network messages whose content, size and timing do not depend on which MPE Envelopes match the Subscriber's keys.
MPE-PUB-012.verify: test. Two clients follow the same Shards for 1 h with 0 and 256 keys. Their request counts and sizes are identical, and a KS test at α = 0.01 does not distinguish their timing.

MPE-PUB-013.title: Fixed pull cadence
MPE-PUB-013.sentence: While retrieving a Shard by pull, the MPE client library shall request new MPE Envelopes every P-PUB-2 seconds.
MPE-PUB-013.verify: test. The standard deviation of inter-request intervals over 1 h is at most 50 ms.

MPE-PUB-014.title: Second-source reconciliation
MPE-PUB-014.sentence: While following a Shard, the MPE client library shall reconcile its received MPE Envelope Identifiers against a second source run by a different Bus Operator every P-PUB-3.
MPE-PUB-014.verify: simulation, one source drops 5% of Envelopes; the client obtains every dropped Envelope the second source holds within 2 x P-PUB-3.

MPE-PUB-015.title: Repair every differing window
MPE-PUB-015.sentence: When reconciliation finds that a Shard window differs from a second source, the MPE client library shall retrieve that complete window, independently of recognition.
MPE-PUB-015.verify: test, every differing window is fetched in full whatever the key set; request captures contain no per-identifier selection of recognized or missing Messages.

MPE-PUB-016.title: Reduced-privacy mode opt-in
MPE-PUB-016.sentence: Where a reduced-privacy retrieval mode is present, the MPE client library shall enable it only after an explicit opt-in by the application for each subscription.
MPE-PUB-016.verify: inspection and test. The default configuration never sends a selector. Opting in for one subscription does not change any other subscription.

MPE-PUB-017.title: Report disclosed Shards
MPE-PUB-017.sentence: The MPE client library shall report, for each subscription, the Shard identifiers it has announced to connected peers.
MPE-PUB-017.verify: test. The reported set equals the GossipSub topic IDs found in captured `SubOpts`.

MPE-PUB-018.title: Recognition key cap
MPE-PUB-018.sentence: If adding a recognition key would raise the Subscriber's key set above P-PUB-4 keys, then the MPE client library shall refuse the addition with a typed `KeyLimit` error.
MPE-PUB-018.verify: test. Adding key P-PUB-4 + 1 returns `KeyLimit`, and the key set is unchanged.

MPE-PUB-019.title: Per-publisher sequence number
MPE-PUB-019.sentence: The MPE client library shall seal in each Message a sequence number one greater than the same publisher's previous Message on the same stream.
MPE-PUB-019.verify: test. 1,000 Messages produce sealed sequence numbers n…n+999.

MPE-PUB-020.title: Logical message identifier
MPE-PUB-020.sentence: The MPE client library shall seal in each Message a logical message identifier that stays the same across every republication of that Message.
MPE-PUB-020.verify: test. Republishing after a failure yields two Envelope identifiers with one logical identifier.

MPE-PUB-021.title: Oversize refusal
MPE-PUB-021.sentence: If a Message exceeds the largest size-class body, then the MPE client library shall refuse the publication with a `TooLarge` error before requesting an Admission Proof.
MPE-PUB-021.verify: test. A body one byte over the limit returns `TooLarge`, and the admission counter is unchanged.

MPE-PUB-022.title: Acceptance before success
MPE-PUB-022.sentence: When the MPE client library submits an MPE Envelope, the MPE client library shall report it `accepted` only after the ingress Bus Node's `Accepted` reply (MPE-NET-049) names that MPE Envelope Identifier.
MPE-PUB-022.verify: test. Against a Bus Node that drops input silently, and against one that answers `PublishFailed{eid}`, the client never reports `accepted`; inspection, `accepted` is documented as ingress application acceptance and queueing, not mesh receipt, storage or finality.

MPE-PUB-023.title: Identical retransmission
MPE-PUB-023.sentence: While an MPE Envelope is unexpired, if no acceptance arrives within P-PUB-5 seconds, then the MPE client library shall resubmit the identical MPE Envelope bytes to a different Bus Node, up to P-PUB-6 Bus Nodes in total.
MPE-PUB-023.verify: test. With the first Bus Node blackholed, the second receives byte-identical bytes, and retransmission stops at expiry.

MPE-PUB-024.title: Publication failure
MPE-PUB-024.sentence: If all P-PUB-6 attempts end without acceptance, then the MPE client library shall report the publication as failed with the error `NotAccepted`.
MPE-PUB-024.verify: test. With all Bus Nodes blackholed, the result is `NotAccepted` after P-PUB-6 × P-PUB-5 seconds.

MPE-PUB-025.title: Closed error set
MPE-PUB-025.sentence: The MPE client library shall return every publish and subscribe failure as one member of a closed, versioned, typed error set.
MPE-PUB-025.verify: inspection of the API. Fault injection maps each of 20 injected faults to exactly one documented error.

MPE-PUB-026.title: GossipSub message identifier
MPE-PUB-026.sentence: The Bus Node shall configure GossipSub to use the message identifier of MPE-NET-010, a domain-separated hash of every MPE Envelope byte, which differs from the MPE Envelope Identifier.
MPE-PUB-026.verify: test. Envelopes differing in one byte get distinct identifiers. Identical Envelopes get the same identifier.

MPE-PUB-027.title: Seen-set until expiry
MPE-PUB-027.sentence: The Bus Node shall keep each accepted MPE Envelope Identifier in its application seen-set until that MPE Envelope's expiry plus P-FMT-4.
MPE-PUB-027.verify: test, replays at 61 s and at expiry - 1 s are not forwarded.

MPE-PUB-028.title: Duplicate is Ignore
MPE-PUB-028.sentence: When the Bus Node receives an MPE Envelope whose identifier is in its seen-set, the Bus Node shall return the GossipSub validation result Ignore.
MPE-PUB-028.verify: test. The forwarding peer's score is unchanged after 100 duplicates.

MPE-PUB-029.title: Expired on arrival is Ignore
MPE-PUB-029.sentence: If an MPE Envelope's expiry is earlier than the Bus Node's clock minus P-PUB-8, then the Bus Node shall return Ignore without storing the MPE Envelope.
MPE-PUB-029.verify: test. An expired Envelope is neither stored nor forwarded, and the sender's score is unchanged.

MPE-PUB-030.title: Back-fill selectors
MPE-PUB-030.sentence: The Store Node shall select back-fill responses only by Shard, time window and continuation cursor.
MPE-PUB-030.verify: inspection of the back-fill request format. It has no Recognition Tag, stream or identifier-list field.

MPE-PUB-031.title: Back-fill completeness
MPE-PUB-031.sentence: When the Store Node answers a back-fill request, the Store Node shall return every MPE Envelope it holds for the requested Shard and window, in pages of at most P-PUB-9 MPE Envelopes, each page ending with a continuation cursor.
MPE-PUB-031.verify: test. A store holding N Envelopes in the window returns exactly N distinct identifiers across all pages.

MPE-PUB-032.title: Refusal is distinguishable
MPE-PUB-032.sentence: If the Store Node does not serve a back-fill request in full, then the Store Node shall return a typed refusal distinct from an empty result.
MPE-PUB-032.verify: test. A store over its rate limit returns `Refused`, never an empty page.

MPE-PUB-033.title: Pull capacity
MPE-PUB-033.sentence: If a Bus Node already serves P-PUB-10 concurrent full-Shard pulls, then the Bus Node shall refuse a further pull with a typed `Busy` response.
MPE-PUB-033.verify: test. Pull number P-PUB-10 + 1 gets `Busy`, and the existing pulls are unaffected.

MPE-PUB-034.title: Busy fail-over
MPE-PUB-034.sentence: When a Bus Node refuses a pull as `Busy`, the MPE client library shall request the pull from another Bus Node in the Bus Registry relay list.
MPE-PUB-034.verify: test. The client is receiving from a second Bus Node within 2 × P-PUB-2.

MPE-PUB-035.title: At-least-once delivery
MPE-PUB-035.sentence: While an unexpired MPE Envelope is retained by at least one configured source that answers the Subscriber's requests, MPE shall deliver that MPE Envelope to the Subscriber's client library at least once.
MPE-PUB-035.verify: simulation, 16 Bus Nodes, 20% churn, 1,000 Envelopes, one answering source per interval; every Envelope reaches every Subscriber.

MPE-PUB-036.title: Envelope deduplication
MPE-PUB-036.sentence: The MPE client library shall pass each MPE Envelope identifier to the application at most once per subscription store.
MPE-PUB-036.verify: test. Each Envelope is injected three times across the three paths, and the application sees it once.

MPE-PUB-037.title: Logical deduplication
MPE-PUB-037.sentence: The MPE client library shall pass each authenticated pair of publisher and logical message identifier to the application at most once per subscription store.
MPE-PUB-037.verify: test. Two Envelopes carrying one logical identifier produce one delivery.

MPE-PUB-038.title: Arrival-order delivery
MPE-PUB-038.sentence: The MPE client library shall deliver Messages in the order it authenticates them, holding no Message back to restore sequence order.
MPE-PUB-038.verify: test. Messages with sequence numbers 3 then 2 are delivered as 3, then 2 marked `late`.

MPE-PUB-039.title: Gap report
MPE-PUB-039.sentence: If a missing sequence number has not arrived P-PUB-7 seconds after a later number from the same publisher and stream, then the MPE client library shall emit a `gap` item naming the publisher and the missing range.
MPE-PUB-039.verify: test. Withholding sequence number 5 produces `gap{5..5}` at P-PUB-7 ± 1 s.

MPE-PUB-040.title: Late fill
MPE-PUB-040.sentence: When a Message arrives whose sequence number lies inside an open gap, the MPE client library shall deliver it as a `late` item.
MPE-PUB-040.verify: test. Releasing the withheld Message yields `late` with sequence number 5.

MPE-PUB-041.title: Gap becomes lost
MPE-PUB-041.sentence: If a gap is still open `L_max` plus P-PUB-8 after it was emitted, then the MPE client library shall mark that gap `lost`.
MPE-PUB-041.verify: test. A `lost` item is emitted at `L_max` + P-PUB-8 ± 1 s.

MPE-PUB-042.title: Caught-up marker
MPE-PUB-042.sentence: When back-fill reaches the newest MPE Envelope the serving Store Node holds, the MPE client library shall emit a `head` item carrying the current cursor.
MPE-PUB-042.verify: test. Exactly one `head` per back-fill, emitted after the last stored Envelope.

MPE-PUB-043.title: Portable inclusive cursor
MPE-PUB-043.sentence: The MPE client library shall resume a subscription from an inclusive cursor defined only by MPE Envelope header fields and wall-clock time, never by a row number or Indexer event `id` local to one source.
MPE-PUB-043.verify: test. Switching mid-back-fill between two Store Nodes with different ingest orders skips no Envelope; on the ledger lane, a resume against a second Indexer, with `id` values translated by the Ledger Adapter (MPE-CON-053), skips no Envelope.

MPE-PUB-044.title: Atomic processing helper
MPE-PUB-044.sentence: Where the application uses the library's idempotent processing helper, the MPE client library shall commit the cursor, the deduplication record and the application's effect in one atomic write.
MPE-PUB-044.verify: test. Kill the process at 1,000 random points (o3 D10 zero-loss chaos test). Each Message's effect occurs exactly once.

MPE-PUB-045.title: Retention exceeded
MPE-PUB-045.sentence: If a subscription resumes from a cursor older than the earliest MPE Envelope any reachable Store Node holds, then the MPE client library shall emit a `gap` item with reason `retention-exceeded` for the unreachable interval.
MPE-PUB-045.verify: test. A client offline for longer than retention receives this `gap` before any Message.

MPE-PUB-046.title: Key erased
MPE-PUB-046.sentence: If a back-fill interval predates the oldest recognition key the Subscriber retains for a stream, then the MPE client library shall emit a `gap` item with reason `key-erased` for that stream and interval.
MPE-PUB-046.verify: test. After erasing the keys of key period 1, back-filling period 1 yields `key-erased`.

MPE-PUB-047.title: Reactions only on explicit call
MPE-PUB-047.sentence: The MPE client library shall submit a transaction or publication that reacts to a Message only when the application explicitly calls a reaction operation.
MPE-PUB-047.verify: inspection. No code path in the library sends a reaction except a reaction call.

MPE-PUB-048.title: External object fetch
MPE-PUB-048.sentence: Where a Message references an external object, the MPE client library shall fetch that object only through a separate operation that the API marks as interest-revealing.
MPE-PUB-048.verify: inspection. Delivering a Message never triggers a fetch, and the fetch operation's type carries the marker.

MPE-PUB-049.title: Unknown schema
MPE-PUB-049.sentence: If an authenticated Message carries a schema identifier the application has not registered, then the MPE client library shall deliver it as an `undecodable` item.
MPE-PUB-049.verify: test. A Message with an unregistered schema arrives as `undecodable` with its sequence number.

MPE-PUB-050.title: Disconnected status
MPE-PUB-050.sentence: If the MPE client library has received no response from any Bus Node or Store Node for P-PUB-11 seconds, then the MPE client library shall emit a `disconnected` status item.
MPE-PUB-050.verify: test. Partitioning the client yields `disconnected` at P-PUB-11 ± 1 s.

MPE-PUB-051.title: Validation before forwarding
MPE-PUB-051.sentence: The Prototype shall run every Bus Node with GossipSub application validation enabled, so that no MPE Envelope payload is forwarded before its validation result.
MPE-PUB-051.verify: test. An Envelope held in validation for 2 s reaches no peer during those 2 s.

MPE-PUB-052.title: Subscriber bandwidth measurement
MPE-PUB-052.sentence: The Prototype shall measure bytes received per Subscriber per day in full-Shard mode at P-PUB-1 = 1 and P-PUB-1 = 8, under the performance area's reference load.
MPE-PUB-052.verify: demonstration. A 24-hour run, with the measured bytes reported against the arithmetic in DEC-PUB-1.

MPE-CON-001.title: Local recognition
MPE-CON-001.sentence: The MPE client library shall perform Recognition Tag matching and decryption on the Consumer's host without sending any recognition key, decryption key, Recognition Tag set or stream identifier to a Bus Node, Store Node or Indexer.
MPE-CON-001.verify: test. Capture all client egress during a subscription and assert that no key, Recognition Tag or stream id appears in it.

MPE-CON-002.title: Whole-Shard retrieval by default
MPE-CON-002.sentence: While in the default reception mode, the MPE client library shall retrieve every MPE Envelope of each subscribed Shard.
MPE-CON-002.verify: test. Compare the set of Envelope ids the source served with the set the client received over 1 h; they must be equal.

MPE-CON-003.title: Recognition-independent requests
MPE-CON-003.sentence: The MPE client library shall make the content and timing of its retrieval requests independent of which MPE Envelopes it recognises.
MPE-CON-003.verify: test. Run two clients with disjoint key sets against the same feed and assert that their request traces are identical apart from transport noise.

MPE-CON-004.title: Opt-in for selective profiles
MPE-CON-004.sentence: Where a selective-retrieval profile is present, the MPE client library shall activate it only when the application passes an explicit opt-in that names that profile.
MPE-CON-004.verify: inspection and test. A configuration without the opt-in must fail to start the profile.

MPE-CON-006.title: Keys only by invitation
MPE-CON-006.sentence: The MPE client library shall add a recognition key only through an explicit application call that supplies an invitation.
MPE-CON-006.verify: inspection of the public API, plus a test that no code path adds keys from received data.

MPE-CON-007.title: Recognition Tag lookahead window
MPE-CON-007.sentence: The MPE client library shall hold, for each subscribed (stream, publisher) pair, the next P-CON-5 expected Recognition Tags.
MPE-CON-007.verify: test. After each recognised Message, assert that the lookahead set holds exactly the next P-CON-5 Recognition Tags.
MPE-CON-007.withdrawn: DEC-003 (salted per-Envelope Tags replace the earlier tag rule)

MPE-CON-008.title: Recognition-window gap
MPE-CON-008.sentence: If no Message from a subscribed publisher is recognised for P-CON-6 while that publisher's Shard carries traffic, then the MPE client library shall emit `gap{reason:"recognition-window"}` for that publisher.
MPE-CON-008.verify: test. The publisher skips 2 × P-CON-5 sequence numbers and the gap appears within P-CON-6 + 10 s.
MPE-CON-008.withdrawn: DEC-003 (salted per-Envelope Tags replace the earlier tag rule)

MPE-CON-009.title: Recognition key cap
MPE-CON-009.sentence: If adding a recognition key would exceed P-CON-7 keys, then the MPE client library shall reject the addition with a typed `KeyLimit` error.
MPE-CON-009.verify: test. Add P-CON-7 + 1 keys and assert the error on the last addition.

MPE-CON-010.title: Generated codecs only
MPE-CON-010.sentence: The MPE client library shall decode sealed bodies only with codecs generated from a schema the application registered.
MPE-CON-010.verify: inspection. No reflective or dynamic decode path exists in the library.

MPE-CON-011.title: Undecodable Messages delivered
MPE-CON-011.sentence: When a recognised Message carries a schema identifier with no registered codec, the MPE client library shall deliver an `undecodable` item that carries the MPE Envelope identifier.
MPE-CON-011.verify: test. Publish under an unregistered schema and assert one `undecodable` item.

MPE-CON-012.title: At-least-once within retention
MPE-CON-012.sentence: While at least one configured source retains an MPE Envelope of a subscribed Shard, the MPE client library shall deliver each Message recognised in that MPE Envelope to the application at least once.
MPE-CON-012.verify: test. Run fault injection with one retaining source and assert that every published Message reaches the handler.

MPE-CON-013.title: Deduplication by Envelope identifier
MPE-CON-013.sentence: The MPE client library shall deliver each MPE Envelope identifier to the application at most once per subscription for the MPE Envelope's lifetime plus P-CON-2.
MPE-CON-013.verify: test. Re-inject the same Envelope after 61 s and again near expiry, and assert a single delivery.

MPE-CON-014.title: Logical deduplication of retries
MPE-CON-014.sentence: The MPE client library shall deliver at most one Message per authenticated logical message identifier to a `processOnce` handler.
MPE-CON-014.verify: test. Publish one logical Message as two Envelopes and assert one handler call.

MPE-CON-015.title: Finality label on every Message
MPE-CON-015.sentence: The MPE client library shall label every delivered Message with exactly one finality label, `gossip` or `final`.
MPE-CON-015.verify: test, every delivered item has exactly one finality label.

MPE-CON-016.title: Meaning of `final`
MPE-CON-016.sentence: The MPE client library shall label a Message `final` only after verifying its MPE Envelope Identifier under an Anchor in Bus Registry state at a finalized block, or its ledger-lane parts against finalized on-chain data confirmed by P-NET-14 independent sources or by block replay.
MPE-CON-016.verify: test with the mock Ledger Adapter: a forged inclusion path, an unfinalized Anchor, an Anchor present only as a `Misc` notification and ledger-lane parts reported by one source only each leave the label at `gossip`.

MPE-CON-017.title: Upgrade notice from gossip to final
MPE-CON-017.sentence: When a Message already delivered as `gossip` becomes covered by a verified finalised Anchor, and for a carried event `MPE-CON-058` and `MPE-CON-059` are also satisfied, the MPE client library shall emit a `finalised{eid}` notice.
MPE-CON-017.verify: test. Publish, observe `gossip`, anchor, and assert one `finalised` notice; an anchored carried event whose transaction is unfinalized, whose fallible segment failed or whose transcript holds different bytes gets no notice.

MPE-CON-018.title: Unanchored notice
MPE-CON-018.sentence: If a Message delivered as `gossip` is not covered by a verified finalised Anchor within P-CON-8, then the MPE client library shall emit an `unanchored{eid}` notice.
MPE-CON-018.verify: test. Suppress the anchorer and assert the notice after P-CON-8.

MPE-CON-019.title: One interface for both labels
MPE-CON-019.sentence: The MPE client library shall deliver `gossip`-labelled and `final`-labelled Messages through the same subscription call and the same item type.
MPE-CON-019.verify: inspection of the API, plus a test that runs the same consumer against the overlay and against the ledger lane.

MPE-CON-020.title: Suspected gap
MPE-CON-020.sentence: When a recognised Message's sequence number leaves a missing lower sequence number for its publisher unfilled for P-CON-1, the MPE client library shall emit `gap{reason:"suspected"}` naming the publisher and the missing range.
MPE-CON-020.verify: test. Drop sequence number n and assert the gap item after P-CON-1.

MPE-CON-021.title: Late fill
MPE-CON-021.sentence: When a Message fills a range already reported as a gap, the MPE client library shall deliver it marked `late`.
MPE-CON-021.verify: test. Delay sequence number n beyond P-CON-1 and assert `gap`, then `late`.

MPE-CON-022.title: No hidden reordering
MPE-CON-022.sentence: The MPE client library shall deliver each recognised Message without waiting for an earlier sequence number from the same publisher.
MPE-CON-022.verify: test. Deliver n+1 before n and assert immediate delivery of n+1.

MPE-CON-023.title: Bounded gap state
MPE-CON-023.sentence: If a publisher's pending-gap state would exceed P-CON-9 sequence numbers, then the MPE client library shall emit `gap{reason:"overflow"}` and discard the oldest pending range.
MPE-CON-023.verify: test. Inject a sequence jump of 10 × P-CON-9 and assert bounded memory plus the overflow item.

MPE-CON-024.title: Caught-up marker
MPE-CON-024.sentence: When back-fill reaches the newest MPE Envelope its source held at subscription time, the MPE client library shall emit one `head` item for that subscription.
MPE-CON-024.verify: test. Run back-fill of 1,000 Envelopes and assert exactly one `head`, placed after the last of them.

MPE-CON-026.title: Closed publish result set
MPE-CON-026.sentence: When a publish call returns, the MPE client library shall report exactly one of `accepted` (the ingress Bus Node completed application acceptance), `final`, or `failed{reason}` from a closed reason set.
MPE-CON-026.verify: test of each failure cause, asserting the matching reason; inspection, `accepted` is not described as remote receipt, storage or finality.

MPE-CON-027.title: Portable cursor
MPE-CON-027.sentence: The MPE client library shall express resume cursors in a form that any source serving the same Shard accepts.
MPE-CON-027.verify: test. Commit a cursor against source A, resume against source B, and assert no Message is lost.

MPE-CON-028.title: Inclusive resume
MPE-CON-028.sentence: When the application subscribes from a committed cursor, the MPE client library shall deliver every retained recognised Message at or after that cursor that is absent from the committed deduplication state.
MPE-CON-028.verify: test. Crash at random points and assert that the union of deliveries equals the set of published Messages.

MPE-CON-029.title: Back-fill by complete window
MPE-CON-029.sentence: The MPE client library shall request back-fill only as complete time windows of a Shard.
MPE-CON-029.verify: test. Inspect back-fill requests and assert they carry only a Shard and a time range.

MPE-CON-030.title: Back-fill window reported
MPE-CON-030.sentence: The MPE client library shall report, through a capabilities call, the back-fill window as the minimum of source retention and local key retention.
MPE-CON-030.verify: test. Set retention to 48 h and key retention to 24 h, and assert a reported window of 24 h.

MPE-CON-031.title: Key-erased gap
MPE-CON-031.sentence: If back-fill covers a period for which the client holds no key, then the MPE client library shall emit `gap{reason:"key-erased"}` for that period.
MPE-CON-031.verify: test. Erase the keys of one key period, back-fill that period, and assert the gap.

MPE-CON-032.title: Retention gap
MPE-CON-032.sentence: If a resume cursor is older than the oldest MPE Envelope held by every configured source, then the MPE client library shall emit `gap{reason:"retention"}` with the uncovered time window.
MPE-CON-032.verify: test. Resume beyond retention and assert the gap with the correct bounds.

MPE-CON-033.title: Atomic processOnce
MPE-CON-033.sentence: The MPE client library shall provide a `processOnce` call that commits the application effect, the cursor and the deduplication state in one atomic write to an application-supplied store.
MPE-CON-033.verify: test. Kill the process between effect and commit and assert one effect after restart.

MPE-CON-034.title: Chaos acceptance
MPE-CON-034.sentence: The Prototype shall complete a P-CON-10-Message run, with random Bus Node restarts, source failovers and client crashes, passing zero lost Messages and zero duplicates to `processOnce` handlers.
MPE-CON-034.verify: test. Run the scripted chaos harness and compare handler logs with the publish log.

MPE-CON-035.title: Delivery model check
MPE-CON-035.sentence: The MPE client library delivery state machine shall satisfy, in a bounded model check, that no committed cursor skips an undelivered retained Message and that `processOnce` passes each logical identifier at most once.
MPE-CON-035.verify: analysis. Quint model including source failover; both invariants hold to the stated depth.

MPE-CON-036.title: Independent sources by default
MPE-CON-036.sentence: The MPE client library shall, by default, retrieve each subscribed Shard from at least P-CON-3 sources run by different Bus Operators.
MPE-CON-036.verify: test. With default configuration, assert connections to P-CON-3 distinct Bus Operators per Shard.

MPE-CON-037.title: Inventory repair
MPE-CON-037.sentence: While subscribed to a Shard, the MPE client library shall compare its MPE Envelope-identifier inventory with a second source every P-CON-4 and fetch every MPE Envelope it lacks.
MPE-CON-037.verify: test. Source A withholds 1% of Envelopes; assert all of them are delivered within P-CON-4 + 10 s.

MPE-CON-038.title: Anchor count check
MPE-CON-038.sentence: When a verified finalised Anchor covers a subscribed Shard window, the MPE client library shall emit `incomplete{window}` if its inventory for that window lacks any anchored MPE Envelope identifier.
MPE-CON-038.verify: test. Withhold one anchored Envelope from all sources and assert the item.

MPE-CON-039.title: No automatic network action
MPE-CON-039.sentence: The MPE client library shall send no network message, acknowledgement or transaction as a consequence of recognising a Message.
MPE-CON-039.verify: test. Compare egress with and without matching keys; it must be identical.

MPE-CON-040.title: Reaction delay
MPE-CON-040.sentence: Where the application submits a reaction through the library's reaction helper, the MPE client library shall delay submission by a uniformly random interval in [0, P-CON-11].
MPE-CON-040.verify: test. Over 1,000 reactions, the delays fit uniform [0, P-CON-11] (KS test, p > 0.01).

MPE-CON-041.title: Off-chain blob fetch is explicit
MPE-CON-041.sentence: The MPE client library shall fetch an off-chain blob referenced by a Message only through a call whose type marks the fetch as observable.
MPE-CON-041.verify: inspection. No implicit blob fetch path exists.

MPE-CON-042.title: Contract reaction by later transaction
MPE-CON-042.sentence: The MPE client library shall provide a reaction builder that produces a Midnight transaction calling a target contract circuit, with the Message supplied as private witness data.
MPE-CON-042.verify: demonstration on a local ledger-9 network, or test against the mock Ledger Adapter.

MPE-CON-043.title: Publisher authorisation in circuit
MPE-CON-043.sentence: The MPE client library's consumption circuit shall assert a publisher signature, under the suite's signature algorithm, over genesis, target contract, action, logical identifier, expiry and payload digest, against a publisher set committed in the target contract's state, and recompute that payload digest from the payload bytes from which it derives every effect input.
MPE-CON-043.verify: test. Wrong key, wrong target, wrong action, wrong genesis, and a valid signature with a changed amount, recipient or other consumed field each fail proof generation, under Ed25519 and, where enabled, JubJub Schnorr; analysis reports rows, proving time and prover-key size of both.

MPE-CON-045.title: Secret-derived consumption nullifier
MPE-CON-045.sentence: The MPE client library's consumption circuit shall derive the consumption nullifier from a secret carried inside the sealed Message, never from the public MPE Envelope identifier alone.
MPE-CON-045.verify: analysis. The consumption nullifier is not computable from public data; a test tries all observed Envelope ids against it.

MPE-CON-046.title: Expiry enforced
MPE-CON-046.sentence: The MPE client library's consumption circuit shall reject a Message whose expiry, taken from its signed expiry or from its anchored creation minute plus P-FMT-3, is earlier than the block time of the reacting transaction.
MPE-CON-046.verify: test. React after expiry under both expiry sources and assert the rejection.

MPE-CON-047.title: Optional publication proof
MPE-CON-047.sentence: Where an application requires proof of publication before a time, the MPE client library's consumption circuit shall verify that the MPE Envelope Identifier is included under a window root whose Anchor-tree leaf passes the Bus Registry's witness-free historic-root check.
MPE-CON-047.verify: test on a local ledger-9 network: the Anchor tree is a `HistoricMerkleTree<12>` with leaf `SHA-256(domain, window, window root)` at slot `window mod 2940`; a forged path fails, a stale accepted root passes, and the reaction carries two contract calls.

MPE-CON-048.title: No infrastructure output as authority
MPE-CON-048.sentence: The MPE client library shall offer no contract-consumption API that accepts output from a Bus Node, Store Node or Indexer as evidence of publisher authorisation.

MPE-CON-049.title: Reactor race test
MPE-CON-049.sentence: The Prototype shall show, with the mock Ledger Adapter, exactly one contract effect when P-CON-12 reactors submit reactions for the same Message concurrently.
MPE-CON-049.verify: test. Count the effects in the mock ledger state; the count must be 1.

MPE-CON-050.title: Ledger paused
MPE-CON-050.sentence: If the Ledger Adapter reports that Midnight rejects user transactions, then the MPE client library shall return a typed `LedgerPaused` error to reaction and ledger-lane publish calls.
MPE-CON-050.verify: test. Set the mock adapter to paused and assert the error.

MPE-CON-051.title: Gossip continues while ledger unavailable
MPE-CON-051.sentence: While the Ledger Adapter reports Midnight unavailable, the MPE client library shall continue delivering recognised Messages labelled `gossip`.
MPE-CON-051.verify: test. Pause the mock ledger and assert continued `gossip` delivery with no `final` labels.

MPE-CON-052.title: Wallet grants
MPE-CON-052.sentence: Where a wallet hosts the MPE client library, the client library shall release a stream's Messages to a DApp only under a grant for that stream issued by the wallet user.
MPE-CON-052.verify: test. A DApp without a grant receives nothing; a DApp with a grant receives only that stream.

MPE-CON-053.title: Ledger lane read
MPE-CON-053.sentence: While the ledger lane is active, the MPE client library shall read ledger-lane MPE Envelopes through the Indexer adapter, filtering by the bus contract address only and resuming from the Indexer's monotonic event `id` as translated by the Ledger Adapter.
MPE-CON-053.verify: test. Inspect Indexer adapter queries; only the address and the `MISC` type appear, and the stored resume point maps to the MPE-PUB-043 cursor.

MPE-CON-054.title: Consumer bandwidth metering
MPE-CON-054.sentence: The MPE client library shall report to the application the bytes received per subscribed Shard per UTC day.
MPE-CON-054.verify: test. The reported count matches captured traffic within 1%.

MPE-CON-055.title: Afternoon test
MPE-CON-055.sentence: The MPE client library shall enable P-CON-13 of 5 developers from outside the team, each using only its documentation, to build a publisher and a crash-resuming subscriber within the P-CON-13 time limit.
MPE-CON-055.verify: demonstration. A timed study whose subscribers then pass a crash-resume check.

MPE-ECO-001.title: No proof-of-work admission
MPE-ECO-001.sentence: The Bus Node shall not use proof-of-work as an admission criterion for an MPE Envelope.
MPE-ECO-001.verify: inspection of the Bus Node validator code path; a test that an Envelope with no work field is accepted when all other checks pass.

MPE-ECO-002.title: DUST is not Bus Operator payment
MPE-ECO-002.sentence: MPE shall not require any party to transfer DUST to a Bus Operator.
MPE-ECO-002.verify: inspection of the client library and Bus Node payment interfaces; no DUST-transfer call exists.

MPE-ECO-003.title: No Midnight transaction per overlay Message
MPE-ECO-003.sentence: The MPE client library shall publish a Message on the overlay without submitting a Midnight transaction for that Message.
MPE-ECO-003.verify: test: publish 1,000 Messages through the Prototype and count zero Ledger Adapter submissions.

MPE-ECO-004.title: Membership registration
MPE-ECO-004.sentence: When the Bus Registry receives a registration transaction carrying a membership commitment, the Bus Registry shall insert that commitment into the membership tree of the current membership period.
MPE-ECO-004.verify: test on a ledger-9 devnet: register, then confirm that the next root contains the leaf; inspection: the only price is the network fee of the registration transaction unless MPE-ECO-056 adds a token price, since a contract cannot receive or observe DUST.

MPE-ECO-005.title: Sponsored registration
MPE-ECO-005.sentence: The Bus Registry shall accept a membership commitment from any caller that pays the registration fee, without requiring that caller to know the admission secret.
MPE-ECO-005.verify: test: a sponsor registers a commitment generated by a separate client, and that client then publishes successfully.

MPE-ECO-006.title: Dedicated admission secret
MPE-ECO-006.sentence: The MPE client library shall generate the admission secret independently of every wallet spending, encryption, signing and session key, either from the operating-system generator or through the `deriveSecret` derivation of MPE-CRY-027.
MPE-ECO-006.verify: inspection of key derivation; a test that the admission secret has no derivation path from any spending, encryption, signing or session key.

MPE-ECO-007.title: Shielded fee payment
MPE-ECO-007.sentence: The MPE client library shall pay Bus Registry registration fees from shielded DUST without attaching unshielded inputs or outputs to that transaction.
MPE-ECO-007.verify: inspection of three devnet registration transactions built by the client: no unshielded offer is present.

MPE-ECO-008.title: Live fee quotes
MPE-ECO-008.sentence: When the MPE client library quotes the DUST cost of a Bus Registry transaction, it shall compute the quote from the `ledgerParameters` of the latest finalized block.
MPE-ECO-008.verify: test with a mocked block whose parameters double the price: the quote doubles.

MPE-ECO-009.title: Insufficient DUST reported before proving
MPE-ECO-009.sentence: If the available DUST is less than the quoted fee, then the MPE client library shall return an insufficient-DUST error before generating any proof.
MPE-ECO-009.verify: test with a balance below the quote: the error is returned and the prover is never called.

MPE-ECO-010.title: Client back-off under chain congestion
MPE-ECO-010.sentence: While the last finalized block's `blockUsage` fullness exceeds P-ECO-9, the MPE client library shall defer membership renewals that are not due within the current membership period.
MPE-ECO-010.verify: test with a mocked block fullness of 60%: renewals due in the next period are not submitted until fullness drops.

MPE-ECO-011.title: Chain-share budget
MPE-ECO-011.sentence: MPE shall consume no more than P-ECO-8 of either the `block_usage` or the `bytes_written` block limit, averaged over 24 h, for Bus Registry registrations, Anchors and ledger-lane parts combined.
MPE-ECO-011.verify: analysis of 7 days of testnet blocks: sum the block bytes and the `bytes_written` of MPE transactions, including ledger-lane parts, and divide each sum by its limit (`bytes_written` is 50,000 B per block).

MPE-ECO-012.title: Admission Proof required
MPE-ECO-012.sentence: If an MPE Envelope lacks an Admission Proof, or its Admission Proof fails verification, then the Bus Node shall return GossipSub `Reject` for that MPE Envelope.
MPE-ECO-012.verify: test: inject a mutated proof; the receiver reports `Reject` and the sender's P₄ counter increases.

MPE-ECO-013.title: Cheap checks before proof verification
MPE-ECO-013.sentence: The Bus Node shall complete the length, admission window, root-window and admission-nullifier duplicate checks on an MPE Envelope before verifying its Admission Proof.
MPE-ECO-013.verify: test with instrumentation: an Envelope with a stale admission window never reaches the verifier.

MPE-ECO-014.title: Admission window freshness
MPE-ECO-014.sentence: If an MPE Envelope's admission window differs from the Bus Node's current admission window by more than P-ECO-6 beyond the admission window boundary, then the Bus Node shall return GossipSub `Ignore` for that MPE Envelope.
MPE-ECO-014.verify: test at offsets of P-ECO-6 − 1 s (accepted) and P-ECO-6 + 1 s (Ignore, no P₄ change).

MPE-ECO-015.title: Root window from supersession
MPE-ECO-015.sentence: If an MPE Envelope's Admission Proof references a membership root that is neither the current root nor superseded less than P-ECO-5 earlier, then the Bus Node shall return Ignore for that MPE Envelope.
MPE-ECO-015.verify: test, with no root update for 2 h the current root still validates; a root superseded P-ECO-5 + 1 s earlier yields Ignore; inspection: the Bus Registry's historic-root check has no time bound, so this Bus Node check alone enforces P-ECO-5.

MPE-ECO-016.title: Committed per-class rate limit
MPE-ECO-016.sentence: The Bus Node shall return Reject for an MPE Envelope of size class c unless its Admission Proof shows a credit index below the class-c per-admission-window limit committed in the membership leaf.
MPE-ECO-016.verify: test, with class-2 limit 4, credit indices 0-3 are accepted and index 4 is Rejected.

MPE-ECO-017.title: Class-bound admission nullifier
MPE-ECO-017.sentence: The MPE client library shall derive each admission nullifier from the admission secret, the Network Identifier, the Bus Registry contract address, the admission window number, the size class and the credit index under the domain-separated hash of the admission proof profile.
MPE-ECO-017.verify: test vectors; two Envelopes of different classes with equal index yield different admission nullifiers, and the same secret, window, class and index under another Network Identifier or another Bus Registry yield a different slope and admission nullifier.

MPE-ECO-018.title: Content-bound Admission Proof
MPE-ECO-018.sentence: The Admission Proof shall bind its rate-limit share to the MPE Envelope identifier, so that two MPE Envelopes with different identifiers under one admission nullifier yield two distinct shares.
MPE-ECO-018.verify: test: produce two Envelopes under one admission nullifier and recover the admission secret from their shares.

MPE-ECO-019.title: Duplicate admission nullifier, same Envelope
MPE-ECO-019.sentence: If an MPE Envelope carries an admission nullifier already accepted with the same MPE Envelope identifier, then the Bus Node shall return GossipSub `Ignore`.
MPE-ECO-019.verify: test: deliver the same Envelope twice from two peers; neither peer's P₄ counter changes.

MPE-ECO-020.title: Equivocation recorded without penalty
MPE-ECO-020.sentence: If an MPE Envelope carries an admission nullifier already accepted with a different MPE Envelope Identifier, then the Bus Node shall return Ignore and record both MPE Envelopes as equivocation evidence.
MPE-ECO-020.verify: test, send two conflicting Envelopes from two peers; no P4 change and the evidence store holds both.

MPE-ECO-021.title: Admission nullifier retention
MPE-ECO-021.sentence: The Bus Node shall retain each accepted admission nullifier for at least P-ECO-7 after acceptance.
MPE-ECO-021.verify: test: restart a Bus Node in the middle of an admission window, then replay a conflicting Envelope; the result is Ignore with the evidence retained, never Accept.

MPE-ECO-022.title: Per-Bus-Node allowance bound
MPE-ECO-022.sentence: The Bus Node shall accept at most one MPE Envelope Identifier per live publication allowance under its local acceptance state.
MPE-ECO-022.verify: simulation with 16 Bus Nodes and conflicting first uses injected at separate nodes: each node accepts at most one identifier per allowance and retains the conflict evidence (MPE-ECO-020); the report states that no network-wide admission count follows from mesh connectivity alone.

MPE-ECO-023.title: Per-peer pre-verification limit
MPE-ECO-023.sentence: If a peer sends more than P-ECO-10 MPE Envelopes per second, then the Bus Node shall drop the excess with GossipSub `Ignore` without verifying their Admission Proofs.
MPE-ECO-023.verify: test: a peer sends 2 × P-ECO-10 Envelopes/s; verifier invocations from that peer stay ≤ P-ECO-10 per second.

MPE-ECO-024.title: Stale Bus Registry view
